<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2da658a8eef28309">Why optimize per-request ad quantity, not just order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranking fills given slots; load chooses their number and affects experience, revenue, and conversion. Estimate marginal response over feasible counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical ad candidates can support different loads for shopping and exploratory requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-367793246886ffd2">Why not always choose the ad count maximizing immediate ad revenue?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Count affects organic experience and conversions as well as revenue. Randomized field experiments estimate count responses; constrained decisions use Lagrangian trade-offs. Correlation logs or ranking proxies are not causal or market evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shopping and navigation queries can react differently to adding one ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14418-adaptive-ad-load/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-367793246886ffd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8fa5c26341b14ab">Why use randomized field evidence instead of comparing high-revenue logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Existing policies choose load based on intent, which confounds revenue differences. Randomized load helps identify intervention effects. Public ranking without interventions cannot establish causal count effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many ads on already high-intent requests does not justify increasing all loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14418-adaptive-ad-load/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8fa5c26341b14ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f2658cd2009f4e6">Why enumerate feasible counts with consistent revenue and conversion definitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score each legal k under inventory and business limits, using comparable revenue and weighted conversion terms. Tune coefficients on validation, not test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not output five ads when zero to three are legal or compare inconsistent per-request/per-ad metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cdm" data-paper-title="Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cdm-24f0cce6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-93a791dccea8c9a7">Why does CDM view diversity as marginal value given the selected prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acdm">Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Value depends on what the list already contains: the first science-fiction item can add variety while the fourth similar one is redundant. MMR combines relevance with redundancy penalties; CDM learns the contextual gain for low-latency serving. Diversity is not a permanent per-item bonus.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third movie by a director may add little if two are already selected, yet be valuable when no work by that director appears.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09021">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93a791dccea8c9a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cdm" data-paper-title="Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ab2a07320495384">Why must CDM&#x27;s student see same-request candidates when distilling an MMR teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acdm">Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMR selection depends on other candidates and redundancy, so isolated item features cannot recover it. CDM learns selection propensity relative to context and combines it with the original recommendation score, transferring costly iterative redundancy reduction to a serving-time scorer. Student approximation need not reproduce the list exactly, and a small local run does not establish production diversity gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A travel clip may be redundant among ten similar clips but distinctive in a cooking list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09021">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ab2a07320495384">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cdm" data-paper-title="Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bc42bf8da4f58b1">What does CDM distillation save compared with online MMR, and what error can it introduce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acdm">Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMR recomputes redundancy against the selected set at each step. The student approximates those decisions quickly, reducing iterative serving cost. It can drift on new candidate distributions or longer lists, so test precision and diversity as well as latency. Proxy gains do not prove exact imitation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One student score can replace repeated comparisons, but the student may underestimate redundancy in a near-duplicate set absent from training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09021">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bc42bf8da4f58b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cdm" data-paper-title="Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-491caed66cdd9445">Why update similarity penalties after selecting each item in the CDM teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acdm">Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MMR penalizes maximum similarity to the current selected prefix. Every addition changes remaining marginal scores; one fixed ranking is not the same contextual decision. Student targets must correspond to the relevant prefix rather than conflating stages in a static item label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After selecting a camping tutorial, reduce the score of its near-duplicate. An empty-prefix score could put both next to each other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09021">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-491caed66cdd9445">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cgr-09571847" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d186e3d75468b242">What decisions does CGR unify by putting generation and reward estimation in one network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model proposes the next item and estimates its business value after insertion, conditioned on the prefix, ad positions, and load rules. Feasibility determines what can be chosen; reward compares legal options. A high reward does not override the rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once the screen reaches its ad cap, even a high-value ad cannot be generated; rank eligible organic items instead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d186e3d75468b242">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6e21fd686061f7">How do CGR&#x27;s decoding-time ad-load constraints differ from deleting surplus ads afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Post-hoc deletions change context and remaining slots, invalidating value estimates for the original prefixes. CGR maintains the feasible set at each generation step and combines it with estimated reward to prune infeasible branches. A high-scoring but unusable list is not a valid result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With at most two ads in five positions, mask ads after using both slots. Generating four ads and deleting two changes the list the system scored.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6e21fd686061f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f174d05b9d0e95e6">How does CGR&#x27;s constraint-aware pruning differ from fixed item ranking in prefix dependence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed item scores do not depend on selected items. CGR updates feasibility and reward at each step, so count and position rules directly change later choices. This reduces repairs but requires accurate value estimates and search budget; one proxy comparison does not prove global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An ad in slot one can force organic content in slot two under spacing rules without changing any ordinary item score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f174d05b9d0e95e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0ea9ddfaee5e68">When should an implementation of CGR update `F(y&lt;t)`?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>After each selection, update the prefix, load, and position state, then construct the next feasible set. Do not generate the whole sequence and assume every prefix was legal. An empty set must terminate or use a defined legal fallback, never silently fill with an invalid item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the final slot has no eligible organic items and the ad cap is reached, report or terminate as defined instead of adding an ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0ea9ddfaee5e68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cohortmix-ts" data-paper-title="Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cohortmix-ts-f84d0507" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-75004509b0ab288c">Why does CohortMix-TS construct a mixed cohort prior before sufficient personal data arrive?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acohortmix-ts">Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DFKI / RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Few personal observations give unstable success estimates. Infer cohort memberships from metadata and mix historical item-arm means to guide initial exploration. Fixed strength limits borrowed confidence so individual feedback can gradually revise it. Shared membership does not imply identical preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Initialize a new user&#x27;s movie success rates from two cohorts, then let a few personal outcomes move the posterior away from the group average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37800">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.37800-cohortmix-ts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75004509b0ab288c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cohortmix-ts" data-paper-title="Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a52b737be11c2a3b">Why does CohortMix-TS use a mixed Beta prior with fixed strength instead of inheriting all cohort counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acohortmix-ts">Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DFKI / RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar cohorts can warm-start a new user, but copying their sample sizes would make personal observations ineffective for too long. Mix cohort means, use controlled pseudocounts, and update on individual exposure feedback. Thompson sampling retains exploration, and local evidence only checks the posterior mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 100,000 cohort events and three personal events, full inheritance drowns out the new user. Fixed prior strength allows personal preference to take over gradually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37800">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.37800-cohortmix-ts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a52b737be11c2a3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cohortmix-ts" data-paper-title="Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea291b7996f80080">How does CohortMix-TS explore differently from always choosing the highest posterior mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acohortmix-ts">Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DFKI / RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Greedy selection ignores uncertainty. Thompson sampling draws from each posterior, giving uncertain but promising arms a chance; more evidence naturally reduces uncertainty. It does not improve every round, and the local three-seed state-transition diagnostic is not recommendation capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A slightly lower-mean, rarely observed arm can sometimes beat a well-known arm in sampled scores, while greedy selection may never try it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37800">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.37800-cohortmix-ts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea291b7996f80080">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cohortmix-ts" data-paper-title="Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc1bab4e714e15fa">Why keep independent Beta counts per new user and exclude previously exposed slate items in CohortMix-TS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acohortmix-ts">Challenges and Solutions for Bandits in the Wild: Warm-Started Mixture Bandits for Cross-Cohort Slate Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DFKI / RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cohort prior only initializes state. Subsequent success and failure belong to that user&#x27;s arm, not every new user. Select from unseen items each round for sequential exploration; unexposed arms do not receive invented failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A comedy click updates only the viewing user&#x27;s success count. An action movie not shown receives no feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37800">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.37800-cohortmix-ts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc1bab4e714e15fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-degr-c402d30b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4515d3bc01040e10">Why feed exploration feedback into DEGR&#x27;s generator rather than just inserting random items at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random insertions collect feedback but do not teach the generator which new content is valuable. Reward-adaptive preference updates retain useful exploration, while same-cohort regularization and inference selection reduce repeats. Lower head share alone is not user benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive feedback on an uncommon outdoor item can inform future generation; random insertion alone starts from scratch each time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4515d3bc01040e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-86fa61ca0bb12fab">Why does DEGR constrain same-cohort representations and adapt preference update strength to exploration reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High per-request scores can still expose similar items repeatedly across requests. Representation regularization reduces directional overlap, adaptive preference updates avoid reinforcing exploration without gains, and inference diversity selection acts on the final list. Spread vectors do not guarantee perceived diversity; measure relevance and exploration feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar shoes may dominate successive sensible lists. Spread candidate directions and separately verify that a new category provides worthwhile exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86fa61ca0bb12fab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce7f25a54ba8e30c">Where do DEGR training diversity regularization and inference diversity-aware greedy selection act?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Squared cosine regularization spreads same-cohort embeddings; greedy selection limits redundancy relative to items already in the current list. Neither substitutes for the other. Excessive regularization separates truly similar items, and overly strong selection can hurt relevance, so ablate each.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spread embeddings do not guarantee variety on one screen; forced screen variety does not fix a representation collapsed around popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce7f25a54ba8e30c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3a307970f00ddbf">How should local DEGR with unchanged NDCG and lower head share be interpreted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs confirm actual preference and diversity-pair updates; report ranking and exposure distribution separately. Zero NDCG gain means no main ranking improvement under this protocol, and slightly lower head share only indicates reduced concentration. Loss presence and update counts are not user value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A less popular list without better relevant positions supports wider exposure, not necessarily happier users.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3a307970f00ddbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-degre-898bafc1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-539fd601ea9cebcc">Why use DeGRe&#x27;s offline cumulative-return evaluator instead of only the next logged item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A point label describes one logged path, not the future list value of alternatives. Beam search uses prefix-dependent lookahead values and distills them into the generator. This expands beyond single-path imitation but can carry evaluator errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A basic tutorial can enable useful advanced items despite a low immediate click probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-539fd601ea9cebcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa97ae7183cd68ce">Why does DeGRe use offline beam lookahead but only a greedy generator online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lookahead scores future list value across prefixes but is costly online. Offline search finds valuable lists and distills value distributions over remaining candidates under each prefix into soft targets. Greedy serving approximates future effects; it learns estimated values, not a guaranteed optimum, and may inherit evaluator bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The highest-scoring first item can force redundant later choices. Offline search can find a better opening and teach it without online permutation search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa97ae7183cd68ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2565b25b45fc835">How are DeGRe dense soft labels richer than distilling only the best beam list?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A winning list supplies one target per step. Dense labels distribute probability across all remaining candidates under that prefix by lookahead value, with list weights emphasizing better trajectories. Denser targets can also spread evaluator bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two good books can both get high target probabilities rather than one winner; a popularity-biased evaluator can still mis-score both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2565b25b45fc835">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64f10e3b26c58fd2">Why mask selected items and normalize DeGRe&#x27;s q_t over candidates remaining under the same prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target represents legal next choices. Repeated items must be excluded, scores must share a prefix, and target softmax and student masks must agree. Greedy serving still updates selected state step by step without a beam.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After movie A is selected, step two distributes probability among other movies. Keeping A in the denominator can train repeated recommendations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64f10e3b26c58fd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:director" data-paper-title="DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-director-8aa08907" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b387bec5d3f4c84">Why does DIRECTOR&#x27;s dynamic index distribution cover all display positions jointly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adirector">DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positions draw from competing candidate sets. Joint transport connects position supply and item allocation, and hard matching creates a feasible slate. Parallel generation reduces sequential dependencies, but still requires relevance and legality checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five positions can all favor the same movie; joint allocation restricts it to its allowed count and assigns other options elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26418-director/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b387bec5d3f4c84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:director" data-paper-title="DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f91ba74c893e498">Why does DIRECTOR combine Sinkhorn with global matching rather than independently choosing each position&#x27;s top item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adirector">DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent predictions can select the same item. Sinkhorn constructs a soft transport plan constrained by row and column marginals; global hard matching then creates a conflict-free list. Soft probabilities alone are not a displayable permutation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all three positions favor A, matching assigns it where most useful and places B and C elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26418-director/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f91ba74c893e498">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:director" data-paper-title="DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-33ef213afb9625c2">Why not decode DIRECTOR&#x27;s Sinkhorn matrix with independent row argmaxes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adirector">DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous soft constraints do not guarantee that independent maxima choose distinct columns. Discrete global matching trades per-position scores for total feasible assignment quality. Temperature and iteration affect approximation, not rowwise legality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both rows favor A at 0.6 over B at 0.4, independent choices conflict; hard matching must give B to one row.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26418-director/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33ef213afb9625c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:director" data-paper-title="DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-adf26f4d49897225">How should DIRECTOR align score matrices and final permutations with candidate IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adirector">DIRECTOR: Dynamic Index-based Recommendation with Transport-Optimized Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rows are positions and columns are candidate identities. Maintain column identity through transport and matching, and retrieve by matched global indexes rather than per-row rank. Explicitly handle duplicate IDs or too few candidates. Local movie proxies do not establish production valid views.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If column two was movie B, indexing a reshuffled candidate table after matching can display the wrong movie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-downstream-rewards-21cba3a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-455bebe20e3ceb57">Why screen immediate behaviors with future engagement in Downstream Rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short-term clicks or saves can be fleeting. Find signals predictive of later activity, then train online-predictable auxiliary heads to account for longer-horizon value. Association remains provisional and each product needs independent verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare accidental image opens with deeper collection exploration before selecting a reward target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-455bebe20e3ceb57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbd417cacfc6a26d">Why screen downstream rewards for future engagement instead of adding all immediate behavior to ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Immediate responses can conflict with satisfaction or amplify noise. Test candidate signals for future engagement and connect only selected heads. Predictive association does not imply causal benefit; evaluate each product and do not add short-term gains as retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opening a large image may be accidental; deeper collection browsing might predict later activity better and is worth checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbd417cacfc6a26d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cf29444b410a58e">How does adding a downstream reward head differ from replacing the ranker?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An auxiliary head preserves the backbone and adds a filtered long-horizon proxy to loss or score fusion across surfaces. Replacement changes more features and serving logic. Model-agnostic integration does not imply shared label semantics or improved component metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A feed can keep relevance and add deep-consumption prediction. Notification weights can differ, and saves are not notification retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cf29444b410a58e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0ff2adff3a1c3c8">Where does future-window information belong when training a downstream reward head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use it for reward screening and supervision, not features beyond request time. Select fusion strength on validation and freeze it. Local future category coverage is a proxy, not platform retention; do not read held-out future events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tomorrow&#x27;s new-topic exploration can label today&#x27;s prediction, but cannot be today&#x27;s input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0ff2adff3a1c3c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dream-c0565aca" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3eb08e15565860a7">Why is DREAM a control plane over an existing recommendation pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intent and Meta Engine infer state and plans. Unified Outlet applies typed bounded parameters to existing retrieval, ranking, and reranking; underlying models still score items. Executability does not establish effectiveness without observed feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Control adjusts category weights and diversification for camping interest without replacing the model that scores every candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3eb08e15565860a7">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fd6aa07542d408de">Why does DREAM translate bounded LLM semantic levels into parameters deterministically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free-form text cannot reliably meet service schemas and ranges. Separate intent, planning, and compilation; the model proposes permitted directions and levels, while one outlet enforces whitelists and bounds. Only verified feedback enters policy memory. The LLM cannot arbitrarily rewrite production or amplify weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An increase-diversity level compiles to a bounded diversification count instead of executing a vague instruction to promote novel content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fd6aa07542d408de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6eacc5f563f85ba1">Why is DREAM&#x27;s shadow online gate not a real production A/B test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent shadow data reduce offline selection overfitting, but the public proxy and fixed reaction environment lack actual user feedback. Production double loops need real experiments. Local relevance improved while concentration rose and novelty fell; report all separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting validation users prevents repeated tuning on one group, but cannot measure adaptation, churn, or week-long live engagement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6eacc5f563f85ba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ad1fc02983bed80">How does DREAM compile semantic levels into legal, bounded parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discrete levels must go through whitelists and deterministic translation. Ranking overrides use original weights and levels; category diversification count is `max(1, default_count + bc)`. Record executed parameters, not an unexecuted proposal, so feedback is attributable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A default count of one plus a level of −2 still compiles to at least one, never a negative serving parameter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ad1fc02983bed80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drem" data-paper-title="DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-drem-6dedd99f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44786acb8838e31e">Why study noise as pairwise preference flips in DrEM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrem">DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rankings depend on relative order; small errors can swap close candidates. Logit perturbation, preference-preserving filtering, and risk correction target this instability, while consistency fusion limits drift. Accurate individual predictions do not guarantee stable pairs, and flip estimates can be wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scores only 0.01 apart can trade first place under small noise despite small individual errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12778-drem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44786acb8838e31e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drem" data-paper-title="DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bde83590cd02c905">Why does DrEM correct preference-flip risk instead of averaging prediction scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrem">DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prediction noise can reverse pair preferences, and averaging can still learn the wrong order. DrEM selects perturbation-stable pairs, corrects the objective for flip risk, and applies consistency fusion to limit ranking drift. Correction assumes a noise estimate and becomes unstable near its boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small CTR perturbation can reverse a close video pair; model that risk rather than trusting the observed order as a clean label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12778-drem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bde83590cd02c905">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drem" data-paper-title="DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cae3e0c16f4d980">What assumptions does DrEM risk inversion add beyond perturbation augmentation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrem">DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Augmentation exposes the model to noise. Inversion combines original and reversed-label losses according to estimated flip risk to recover the clean objective. It needs valid risk estimates and a nonsingular denominator; errors leave bias or amplify variance. Noise alone is not inversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correcting a true 40% flip rate as 20% remains biased. Random perturbations do not supply the inversion coefficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12778-drem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cae3e0c16f4d980">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drem" data-paper-title="DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8670300d1dfc49e8">Why separately check probability-to-logit conversion and `1−2ρ` in DrEM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrem">DrEM: Dual-Side Robust Ensemble Ranking from Noisy User Preference Predictions in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probabilities of zero or one cause infinite logits, while flip rate ρ near one half makes the inversion denominator singular. Document handling rather than silently producing huge gradients, and verify filtering, correction, and consistency fusion separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coin-flip preference contains no recoverable signal merely because it is divided by a tiny denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.12778-drem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8670300d1dfc49e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drl-put" data-paper-title="Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-drl-put-ba6d0f54" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4769e145ec181242">Why make utility weights the action instead of generating items in DRL-PUT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrl-put">Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Existing CTR, CVR, relevance, and revenue models score candidates. The policy chooses a controlled mix, and feedback evaluates the induced list, not isolated causal item effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 7:2:1 versus 4:3:3 mix changes order while leaving item embeddings and the click model unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drl-put" data-paper-title="Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
