<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a39e4cbdc0eedaf9">Does DRL-PUT learn which items to recommend or how to combine utility scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrl-put">Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions specify weights for relevance, CTR, CVR, and related scores. A request-conditioned policy combines existing predictors, while offline updates correct action distribution differences using logging probabilities. Rarely logged weights lack evidence for claims of live optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep ad representations fixed but emphasize relevance for exploration and conversion for purchase intent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drl-put" data-paper-title="Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5788a31ee9ff996">How does DRL-PUT off-policy updating differ from fitting high-reward logged examples directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrl-put">Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs are generated by μ and target choices follow π; the probability ratio addresses differing action frequencies. Without it, frequently tried actions dominate. Valid support and logging are required, extreme ratios increase variance, and public proxies are not randomized ad logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the old system nearly always emphasized CTR, most high rewards may follow that choice without showing alternatives are worse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.05292-drl-put/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5788a31ee9ff996">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:drl-put" data-paper-title="Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96e89b6778bf510d">Why must action identities match logged propensities in DRL-PUT&#x27;s `π/μ`?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adrl-put">Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep executed weights, behavior probability, context, and reward tied to one event. With μ=0, no support exists; a tiny replacement does not enable unbiased extrapolation. Baseline b cannot read test outcomes, and final lists alone cannot reconstruct the update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Logging the propensity of 4:6 for an executed 7:3 mix gives the wrong gradient multiplier despite a genuine reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<span id="paper-recommendation-dual-rerank-e775c831" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-002570e2a9cfb086">Why does Dual-Rerank pair an AR teacher with an NAR student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher learns prefix and order dependencies item by item. The student estimates positions in parallel using distilled distributions and utilities, avoiding teacher calls at serving. Check deduplication and position consistency rather than assuming full teacher capability is preserved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The student can learn basic-then-advanced tutorial ordering and score positions together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-002570e2a9cfb086">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a932ffec24fac84">How does Dual-Rerank&#x27;s parallel NAR student absorb an autoregressive teacher&#x27;s ordering dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The AR teacher models prefix-dependent item interactions at sequential serving cost. Ranking distribution and utility distillation compress its ordering preferences into parallel rank estimates. The student approximates rather than recomputes every prefix-dependent decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn that a tutorial before equipment raises list value and emit the list once; novel combinations may still differ from the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a932ffec24fac84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6793aecc3c187e00">What trade-off does utility distillation allow beyond matching AR probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL matches distributions, while utility lets quality and serving constraints enter the student&#x27;s objective so it can deviate where appropriate. Bad utility proxies can harm quality, and a latency term is not proof of actual speed. Measure both contributions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The student may preserve high-value list relationships without matching tail probabilities exactly; speed alone can reward irrelevant output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6793aecc3c187e00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-843d902d26c1e784">Why align candidates, positions, and masks for Dual-Rerank&#x27;s AR–NAR KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher is prefix-constrained and the student may see all candidates in parallel. Compare the same event space with matching masks for padding and selected items and matching candidate identities. Copying final teacher scores to each position does not teach order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A step-two teacher excludes the movie at step one; a full-pool student distribution has a different denominator until explicitly aligned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-843d902d26c1e784">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-35e394cf0e16a8ef">Why is a full-page GenPage action closer to the homepage objective than per-item prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Page utility depends on content types, layout, and interactions. Individually relevant items can form repetitive pages. Condition generation on the selected prefix and evaluate overall reward, accepting harder search and credit assignment without assuming global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A page of one movie franchise can be individually relevant but provide no exploration entry points.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb061952942a7382">Why does GenPage post-train full-page generation on long-term reward rather than simply imitate past pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cloning or SFT reproduces logged display behavior, not necessarily long-term effects of positions and combinations. Page-level reward evaluates the full action while post-training respects business feasibility and cold start. Public proxy lists are not production long-term retention evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Imitation copies rows of popular items. Adding novel content requires real evidence of sustained exploration, not just more diverse titles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb061952942a7382">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6cf9fc644ec1b04d">What evidence do GenPage WBC/SFT and long-term RL use?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weighted demonstrations build a usable policy from existing pages. RL adjusts beyond imitation using reliable long-term environments and rewards. Movie proxies do not recover retention, and business and cold-start constraints need separate enforcement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn a sensible layout quickly from logs; explore more only when long-term feedback supports it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6cf9fc644ec1b04d">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f31e6dc5dcbd000">Why is GenPage&#x27;s MovieLens core not Netflix&#x27;s production full-page implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public data lack real layout, multiple content formats, and long-term rewards. The fixed candidate protocol only checks actual implemented proxy states, constraints, and updates; a ranked list is not a homepage. Preserve negative local results independently of paper gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A ten-movie list has no carousel, copy, or multi-day reactions and cannot verify the production UI or retention policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0293f9dc765bc20a">Why separate GESE title exploration from personalized selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate a relevant, diverse, faithful pool, then choose by current user and context. The selector cannot repair a pool lacking faithful options, and catchy wording does not imply satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Title variants can emphasize method, setting, or conclusion, but none may invent results absent from the article.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-31ed3abf673cb8cf">Why does GESE explore diverse faithful titles and then select one for current context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fixed title lacks personalization; online free generation costs compute and can misrepresent content. Reusable candidate creation and real-time selection are separate, and diversity cannot justify false claims. Fixed-candidate local scoring verifies selection only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A documentary can have faithful titles about photography or natural history, but not invented action scenes for clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31ed3abf673cb8cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-068e2515ee4f87c1">How does GESE allocate compute compared with using an LLM to write each user&#x27;s title in real time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reusable candidates amortize expensive generation across requests and leave real-time adaptation to a lightweight selector. Per-user generation is more flexible but adds latency, repeated cost, and consistency risks. Pre-generation limits coverage; deterministic local scoring does not establish production speed or quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate five faithful angles once and let a thousand users run only selection. An angle outside the pool cannot be created by the selector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-068e2515ee4f87c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21b38b3c2ed12207">Why is GESE&#x27;s local candidate scorer not full LLM generation training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It uses deterministic relevance, diversity, faithfulness, and contextual selection to validate the selection mechanism, not full set generation or production post-training. Report the implemented operators and negative results; paper online metrics are not local measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting among five hand-written titles verifies a selector, not a model&#x27;s ability to generate those faithful titles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21b38b3c2ed12207">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-glorank-9a7d512b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5adb644fca5330fb">Why can GloRank select items outside the local candidate pool with global SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global identifiers define actions over the catalog instead of the current list, adding nomination to reranking. This expands coverage while increasing search, legal mapping, and list-objective difficulty. Fixed-candidate assumptions no longer describe all results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A niche book omitted from five popular local candidates can be nominated globally if legal and relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5adb644fca5330fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bebbdd575e1cb4b">Why does GloRank move beyond ordinary reranking when it replaces local IDs with global SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local IDs only address upstream candidates. Global SIDs allow a broader catalog, so training learns nomination as well as list utility. Larger action spaces complicate search and legality and require evaluation different from closed-pool reranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Index 11 is invalid in a ten-item local list; a global code can nominate a new item only if it maps to a serveable catalog entry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bebbdd575e1cb4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-82506a319bcd80dd">Why state candidate access when comparing global generation and local reranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-catalog generation can improve coverage independently of ordering. Define full or local evaluation, legal mappings, and reward protocols. Different access is not a single-component ablation, and preserve local negative results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding the right book outside a fixed pool does not show a better reranker; the local model could not choose it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82506a319bcd80dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-418c8e5487031517">Why can&#x27;t request-local indexes replace global SIDs in GloRank listwise SFT and group rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local indexes change with candidate order and cannot identify catalog items consistently. Train and decode mapped global paths, and score actual generated identities without fixing invalid codes using test answers. Do not claim full global language training from a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Index three can mean camera in one request and tent in another, so it is not a stable global token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-418c8e5487031517">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harmonrank" data-paper-title="Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-harmonrank-1abfcd00" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c91d11da9694e889">Why move from classification scores to rank relationships in HarmonRank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharmonrank">Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different target base rates and scales can dominate arithmetic fusion. Differentiable rank-sum/AUC first emphasizes each task&#x27;s internal order, then learns task dependencies. Ranking loses absolute value magnitude rather than preserving every business unit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A purchase score can be numerically tiny but still rank items meaningfully, without saying how much more value one brings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02955-harmonrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c91d11da9694e889">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harmonrank" data-paper-title="Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-460ed145b6ab2671">Why align task ranks before fusing raw predicted probabilities in HarmonRank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharmonrank">Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different base rates and scales make raw fusion sensitive to calibration and sparsity. Differentiable rank-sum learns within-task order; inter-task attention models dependencies such as purchases and comments before unified ranking. Rank alignment discards magnitude and is not a general probability calibrator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Purchase probabilities are much smaller than click probabilities; ranking candidates within each task reduces raw-scale dominance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02955-harmonrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-460ed145b6ab2671">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harmonrank" data-paper-title="Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2689dff0a475a4a9">How does inter-objective self-attention handle conflicts differently from fixed fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharmonrank">Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed coefficients impose a global trade-off. Attention learns dependencies and conditional combinations, increasing flexibility but risking domination by frequent objectives. Check by task and example; the local negative result does not establish quality benefits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A highly clicked but rarely purchased item can be treated differently from one high on both, instead of applying the same 7:3 ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02955-harmonrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2689dff0a475a4a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harmonrank" data-paper-title="Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-205f2c06bfda2ec2">Why require both classes and identify invalid tasks in a soft-AUC batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharmonrank">Rethinking Multi-objective Ranking Ensemble in Recommender System: From Score Fusion to Rank Consistency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>AUC needs comparable positive-negative pairs; one-class slices must be masked or reported not estimable, not scored as perfect. Align candidate IDs across tasks. Temperature and sampling affect the differentiable approximation and its gradients, not actual full-data AUC.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An all-zero purchase batch has no pairs and must not send a perfect score into task fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.02955-harmonrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-205f2c06bfda2ec2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hcub-b171df10" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d31f882b2fed638">Why choose context-tree granularity dynamically in HCUB?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fine nodes are relevant but sparse; parents are better sampled but coarse. Reward inheritance handles cold starts and yields to local data. Tree design and mixing affect bias, so more partitions do not ensure accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Borrow a parent estimate after two events, then rely more on the child after 100 observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d31f882b2fed638">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92bc40ad4dfe9d20">Why does HCUB inherit parent rewards in sparse contexts while preserving exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fine-grained estimates have high variance. Parent rewards give a stable starting point, and local data gradually gain weight. Choose by incremental value plus uncertainty to avoid early lock-in. Hierarchical sharing can mask minorities, so do not replace all local evidence with parent averages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sparse device group borrows regional experience until feedback reveals its own preferences, with exploration helping discover that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92bc40ad4dfe9d20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31e5f1063f754e80">How does HCUB incremental reward plus UCB differ from greedy absolute CTR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Increment measures change relative to a reference, and the exploration bonus addresses uncertainty. CTR greedy favors already responsive groups. Increment needs suitable causal data; confidence bonuses are not identification, and movie proxies do not establish interventions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An active group might click anyway, while a less active group may respond more to the action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31e5f1063f754e80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba7a862fd90fa644">How should HCUB avoid propagating one sparse child&#x27;s feedback to every node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Define local statistics and parent prior update scopes. Reading a mixture does not copy one outcome across the tree. Use defined η and uncertainty, retain action identities, and do not invent failures for unobserved arms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Update a child&#x27;s observed success and permitted ancestor aggregates without marking every sibling as a success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba7a862fd90fa644">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:higr" data-paper-title="HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-higr-d87ebf0f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-75d3a4b1b9164993">Why choose semantic clusters before items in HiGR&#x27;s page generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahigr">HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchy divides a large space into coarse interests and precise identities, enabling composition across groups. Wrong coarse codes restrict later candidates, and apparent diversity does not prove relevance. Evaluate both quantization and whole-page utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose tutorial, tool, and example groups before specific items, while recognizing a wrong entertainment branch can remain diverse but irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24787">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24787-higr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75d3a4b1b9164993">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:higr" data-paper-title="HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f29b5cfbf4107740">Why does HiGR need whole-page preference alignment after choosing semantic clusters then items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahigr">HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchical codes make identification easier but individual relevance does not ensure useful order or complementarity. The Hierarchical Slate Decoder generates coarse-to-fine choices; ORPO reshapes combinations from preferred and rejected pages. Evaluated preferences do not guarantee long-tail or utility gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sports clusters can yield only near-duplicate shoes; page preferences can add socks or training content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24787">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24787-higr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f29b5cfbf4107740">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:higr" data-paper-title="HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d13d7f938c1fcfbc">How does HiGR ORPO preference evidence differ from page-level SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahigr">HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT imitates positive pages. ORPO compares preferred and rejected page odds to teach relative composition. Preference and quantization biases remain, and local NDCG declined; report it with head-share changes instead of declaring overall improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An equally relevant but more complementary page can beat a repetitive one; a winner-only target provides no explicit relative signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24787">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24787-higr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d13d7f938c1fcfbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:higr" data-paper-title="HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-29d8f706697c4551">Why define HiGR sequence probabilities and numerical boundaries before calculating log odds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahigr">HiGR: Industrial-Scale Hierarchical Generative Slate Recommendation Framework in Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Page probability is a product of conditional token probabilities and can underflow; use stable log-space arithmetic for both the joint and its complement. Arbitrary scores are not probabilities. Match hierarchical mappings and repetition constraints to page identity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Taking logs after a long-page probability rounded to zero fails; silently replacing the sequence probability with a length average changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24787">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24787-higr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29d8f706697c4551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ltv-video-ranking-a90843c2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec0e6682983c183a">Why does LTV Video Ranking correct position before assigning long-term session value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position affects views and interactions. PDQ aligns outcomes across positions before aggregating session and cross-day creator value to avoid confusing exposure with contribution. Quantile correction relies on distributional assumptions and does not remove all exposure confounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first video is easier to see than the fifth. Match position conditions before attributing subsequent consumption to creator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec0e6682983c183a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d76f2f5cf0db518c">Why correct position bias before including session and cross-day creator value in LTV video ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top positions generate more views, so raw engagement can reward exposure rather than long-term contribution. Correction aims for comparable feedback before session attribution and creator-cycle objectives assign longer-horizon value. Quantile mappings and attribution have assumptions; their combined score is not identified causal retention lift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A creator always shown first gets more clicks than one shown lower. Align exposure opportunity before judging who drives sustained consumption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d76f2f5cf0db518c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c2041aa0f275a2e">How does long-term creator value differ from ranking by seconds watched on one video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watch time rewards immediate consumption; a cross-day creator objective may reward consistent supply rather than one attention-grabbing video. Define how to combine the two and check whether the long-term proxy favors incumbent creators. The public proxy lacks real creator cycles and does not establish retention or ecosystem gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A sensational video can hold attention once, while a reliable series brings people back for days. Watch time alone can miss the latter contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c2041aa0f275a2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-284c94dfb453b29c">Why must PDQ distinguish the original position distribution from the reference distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Find the outcome&#x27;s quantile in its original position&#x27;s conditional distribution, then invert it in a common reference distribution. Inverting in the original distribution would nearly recover the original value. Fit distributions from allowed data and do not tune on future test behavior; without real position logs this is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Map a fifth-position video&#x27;s top-decile watch time to the reference position&#x27;s top-decile value, not back to the fifth position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-284c94dfb453b29c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-maps-creative-255b1b1c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9827f5fc7350a04f">Why does MAPS split creative generation into Profile, Scripter, Director, and Reflector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The roles extract needs and style, write product messaging and scenes, execute video, and route feedback. This localizes errors rather than rebuilding all stages. Role names do not confer capability; real semantic models, video generation, and a credible environment are needed. The local scope is review-only for cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fix copy that overclaims, or fix video execution that violates the script, rather than forcing the profiling agent to rewrite a correct preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9827f5fc7350a04f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d63df493a0c089e0">Why does MAPS&#x27;s Reflector separate profile errors from script errors and route a minimal edit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Poor feedback can arise from misunderstanding the user or from messaging and factual mistakes. Rebuilding everything wastes compute and can damage correct stages. Role attribution targets the relevant stage and keeps profile, script, and video generation auditable. Mixed rewards cover structure, personalization, and factuality. Large models and private environments make this review-only; there is no keyword substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fix a script that overstates product performance when the profile is right. If the gift recipient was misunderstood, polishing shots cannot fix targeting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d63df493a0c089e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78415cab72cfc051">What does MAPS&#x27;s mixed reward measure that keyword counts cannot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structure includes scene roles and physical plausibility; semantic judges score personalization and product consistency. Keyword coverage cannot detect contradictions or user fit. A proxy can test interfaces but is not algorithm evidence. Reward weights do not guarantee judge quality, and text scores differ from creative outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Durable&#x27; and &#x27;perfect for you&#x27; can satisfy keywords while calling ordinary shoes fireproof. Product consistency must check facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78415cab72cfc051">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04085df67bb7bfc8">Why doesn&#x27;t MAPS perform effective RL when group feedback never differs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scripts in the same context need different rewards. Identical rewards yield zero centered advantage and no preference direction. The actual judge and video pipeline also matter. The source explicitly avoids a keyword proxy; evaluating the formula alone does not reproduce training or the environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If a crude rule gives all four scripts full marks, an optimizer call cannot teach which is more personalized or establish improved four-agent video creation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04085df67bb7bfc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-metastrategy-1088d4bd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cb0e2b1dcb6379f">Why put objective weights, preferences, constraints, and position rules into typed JSON in MetaStrategy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed scorer is hard to steer on demand, and free text is difficult to execute reliably. Typed parameters separate semantic planning from deterministic ranking. Validity is only a format gate; still check ranges, replay, and feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raising a freshness weight with a placement limit is executable, unlike &#x27;show more new items,&#x27; but it may still be bad for the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09440-metastrategy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cb0e2b1dcb6379f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-931667540866622d">Why does MetaStrategy generate typed policies rather than final item order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Typed objective weights, category preferences, and position constraints are explicit and compiled deterministically against real candidates. This bounds execution and makes failures auditable. The LLM interprets intent and the compiler executes it; evaluate them separately. Valid JSON proves interface compliance, not utility, and self-scores do not replace replay feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For less repetition, emit a bounded category-diversity rule. If matching candidates are absent, expose the limit rather than inventing items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-4de5dd9640bbf81d">What is auditable and reusable in MetaStrategy compared with direct item-list generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A list is bound to its candidates, whereas a policy can be inspected and reapplied after candidates change. Compiler expressiveness limits which preferences it can encode. The typed-bundle proxy is not full production distillation or equivalent intelligence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;At most one per author&#x27; works across candidate lists; a fixed ten-book list goes stale. The rule cannot interpret all content semantics.</p>

Bind the schema and defaults to actual output and record failures rather than guessing intent. A JSON file does not implement online reward routing or teacher–student OPD.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ogr" data-paper-title="Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
