<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-14454e397408092b">Why does OGR&#x27;s TUSID encode semantics and collaboration instead of only quantizing content?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aogr">Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content generalizes to new items; collaborative codes preserve consumption relations. GL2P plans a slate and SPA adapts from feedback, distinct from coding. Richer codes can conflict and do not guarantee better pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Visually different items bought together can connect via collaboration; new items can borrow semantic structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ogr" data-paper-title="Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e953ac0fa93e88c7">Why fuse semantic and collaborative codes before conservative slate optimization in OGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aogr">Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic codes share content structure and collaborative codes capture behavior relations; encoding organizes the generative space. Planning treats a slate as one action to model item combinations, and conservative feedback updates limit drift from supervision. Representation, joint action, and stable learning are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four individually strong shoes can be redundant, while a slate can combine shoes, socks, and a pack without jumping to an unfamiliar combination for one reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ogr" data-paper-title="Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6bca16b182e0c0a">Why does conservative SPA keep an SFT anchor rather than maximize reward freely?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aogr">Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse or misspecified rewards can favor extreme slates. KL limits drift from supervised behavior, trading improvement freedom for stability without fixing bad rewards. Local NDCG and Hit moved in different directions, not universal gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Novelty alone may favor irrelevant tail items; SFT preserves interest, but excessive constraint may block exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ogr" data-paper-title="Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-c51a2b6ad730034d">Why must OGR&#x27;s R(Y) and KL compare the whole slate rather than one item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aogr">Once Generated, Ranked: End-to-End Generative Slate Recommendation with Unified Semantic-Collaborative IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Y is the slate, so reward, generation probability, and reference must apply to the same list or defined token decomposition with consistent IDs and deduplication. Mean item reward misses interactions and fixed score mixing is not policy updating. State the actual local path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Five individually relevant duplicates can have high mean item score but poor slate value.</p>

<h2 id="qa-de9d8b1bc0e5a79f">Why does PIANO&#x27;s IAN read the entire candidate list?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choice depends on substitutes and competitors on the page. Aggregation conditions item CTR/CVR on the current alternatives, while query-related history represents needs. This differs from static item value and changes when the list changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A mid-priced shoe can look practical among expensive models but not among cheap ones.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c7a8b51cd4bdf5b">Why extract query-relevant history and condition item predictions on the entire slate in PIANO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History selection captures current search intent; slate aggregation tells each CTR/CVR prediction which alternatives surround the item. They model different relationships. A change in candidates can change every score, so these are not independent cacheable item values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A hiking-shoe search reads outdoor history, while the same shoe has different appeal among premium models versus beginner models.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-4f6aa8a43da07d5d">How does PIANO list conditioning change caching and evaluation versus pointwise CTR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent scores can be reused for fixed user–item inputs; list-conditioned scores also depend on candidate membership. Extra context may help competition modeling but costs compute and is distribution-sensitive. The public proxy was negative, not universal superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Removing the cheapest item can alter all other predictions. Reusing old scores would ignore the new IAN context.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-1e1faf71d3bafef6">How avoid leaking gold target position through PIANO list aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The candidate list is allowed, but never order or flag it using real clicks. Labels enter loss only. Mask padding and candidate count, and query only past history. Otherwise IAN can learn a position shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Always putting the correct product first inflates test results if that layout is repeated; use a serving-equivalent unlabeled list.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6d3443f9095014d">Why use component-specific towers for images, titles, and layout in PinDCO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Components differ in modality and statistics. Separate encoders retain roles before combining them to predict increments for one base ad. Interaction remains necessary to score combinations. A predicted lift is not randomized causal evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Changing a title and changing image shape have different effects; an attractive image can still mismatch the copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d06f2355b72efe84">Why predict creative lift over a base ad and penalize pixel use in PinDCO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base scores already capture product–user match; increments isolate predicted image, title, and layout effects. Tall creatives consume more feed space, so a pixel adjustment weighs value against footprint. Exploration gathers new feedback. The local pixel-free proxy is not causal layout evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A taller image can gain clicks but displace content. Prefer it only when added value offsets space cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d06f2355b72efe84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ae9e5ad97be3805">How does PinDCO ε-greedy help new creatives compared with giving all traffic to historical winners?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Greedy exposure starves new creatives of evidence. Limited random exploration provides less-selected feedback for component learning, but costs traffic and does not remove all confounding. Pixel adjustment separately controls space; retain catalog and factual safeguards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new title with no clicks may simply lack exposure. Explore modestly without showing clearly misleading copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ae9e5ad97be3805">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21c31e3b63c31f20">Why preserve PAM clipping and the precise definition of relative aspect ratio r?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>P(r)=clip(1−tanh(k(r−1)),0,1) penalizes tall creatives within a legal range and multiplies base objective O. Inverting the ratio or omitting clipping changes the behavior. Local content norm is a pixel-free proxy, not real layout efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If r means height over width, using width over height reverses the screen-space penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21c31e3b63c31f20">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-299e1034b7d7ddc7">Why can primal–dual decoding work without retraining a generator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Serving search combines original relevance with auxiliary scores and updates multipliers while leaving weights unchanged. It cannot create knowledge missing from the candidates or generator. Measure runtime, relevance loss, and constraint satisfaction separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Increase new-author weight when lacking one, without changing the base model&#x27;s scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1804a3b129c4958e">Why adjust primal–dual decoding multipliers dynamically rather than add a fixed diversity bonus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights cannot react to remaining slack. Per-position scoring combines model relevance with auxiliary contribution and adjusts multipliers so later choices can compensate. No retraining is needed, but candidate availability and local search limit results, with possible relevance loss and no guarantee for arbitrary hard constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If four of five slots include only one new author but two are desired, raise the last-slot incentive; reduce pressure once satisfied.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1804a3b129c4958e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0779bc4cfc3e4265">Can primal–dual soft objectives replace hard eligibility constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Multipliers shift preferences but unavailable or out-of-catalog items must be explicitly excluded. A larger multiplier cannot create feasible items. Soft optimization trades objectives within hard eligibility; no arbitrary-constraint guarantee is reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Encourage new authors softly, but mask out-of-stock items rather than let them win after a penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0779bc4cfc3e4265">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d3a9288628b2b06">Why keep mirror-descent multipliers nonnegative and control exponent ranges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonnegative multipliers preserve penalty direction, and positive initialization with multiplicative updates preserves sign. Large steps can overflow or become extreme. Match auxiliary units, R/K targets, and relevance scores; follow actual probability/logit conventions rather than interchanging them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raw seconds mixed into probabilities can dominate. Repeated exponential increases can pursue quota at the expense of relevance even without an error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d3a9288628b2b06">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfcea21c081d6ffb">Does Pareto non-dominance in PRL-PUTS require improvement on all objectives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A policy remains when none is at least as good on every goal and better on at least one. Different Repin/P2P trade-offs can be nondominated. Suitability still depends on business needs, constraints, and estimation error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: (8,3) and (6,5) trade off while (5,2) is dominated. The first two are not necessarily better than production.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b30234155339f02">Why preselect PRL-PUTS weights via two Q heads and a Pareto sweep?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each head estimates a business utility and weight mixtures choose trade-offs. An offline sweep drops dominated strategies and yields a governable frontier; serving can switch weights without swapping models. Q estimation error and drift make offline non-dominance insufficient for online superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep one policy strong in saves and another strong in deeper interactions, and discard one worse in both rather than testing arbitrary weights on traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b30234155339f02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5dfcbf1bdbb87b31">What choices does Pareto sweeping retain beyond one highest weighted PRL-PUTS score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One weighting selects one compromise. Sweeping and removing dominated strategies retains options for changing goals. Offline noise can create false frontier points, so uncertainty and online tests matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep stronger-save and stronger-engagement policies, but reject one worse on both rather than promoting it for an arbitrary score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5dfcbf1bdbb87b31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-bd0619af50c1211a">Why hold Q model and action-space versions fixed when switching PRL-PUTS weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight effects are identifiable only over the same comparable Q values and action set. Keep α in range and record each head&#x27;s units and reward definition. A fixed local scorer does not reproduce full long-term Q-learning and online governance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Switching 70/30 to 50/50 while retraining a Q head confounds attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:psg" data-paper-title="PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-bd4316b465920770">Does lossless PSG expansion mean pair and item models have the same probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apsg">PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mapping recovers both items and their order for a given pair; the scorer and search distribution can still change. Fewer steps do not imply equal training error, coverage, or quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Packing A B C D as AB and CD recovers it exactly, but the new model can prefer other pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:psg" data-paper-title="PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-17163889d7416526">Why do PSG pair tokens reduce steps but need internal order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apsg">PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each token jointly models two positions and can be losslessly expanded, halving autoregressive steps for even lengths. Pair order affects display and future conditions, while cross-pair duplicates can invalidate the slate. Some complexity moves to the larger pairing/scoring space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Six items take three ordered pairs. Coffee machine then beans differs from beans then machine; another pair containing the machine needs duplicate handling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:psg" data-paper-title="PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36598c3f06a42d49">What dependency can PSG pair scoring capture beyond parallel individual item heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apsg">PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint scoring evaluates two items and their order as one action, modeling complementarity. Parallel independent heads may not. The pair action space can be large, and the proxy regressed, so half-length alone is not lossless speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camera plus lens can be better than two redundant high-scoring cameras, but all possible pairs outnumber individual items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26427">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.26427-psg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36598c3f06a42d49">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:psg" data-paper-title="PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-e93e622c0c622dc8">Why deduplicate across PSG pairs instead of only within each pair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apsg">PSG: Pair-Space Generation for Efficient Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local uniqueness does not prevent repeats across a slate. Check new pairs against the selected prefix and preserve internal order when expanding. Define odd lengths, leftovers, and empty legal sets instead of repeating items to fill slots.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camera–lens and camera–bag are each unique internally but repeat the camera after expansion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-d6adce1daee6cd20">Why combine structured property attributes with conversational needs instead of just listing prose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Descriptions can be vague; structured price, size, and commute specify constraints, while dialogue gives priorities and trade-offs. Set statistics add context. Language reasoning cannot replace factual attribute validation or rewrite facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Both listings say convenient; five versus twenty minutes to transit resolves a ten-minute requirement.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93d88b0ec85364b8">Why include candidate-set statistics in real-estate LLM reranking rather than score each listing independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conversation needs can trade off budget, commute, and space across structured data and text. Set statistics provide current alternatives for relative decisions beyond vector similarity. List changes can invalidate scores, and reranking cannot recover missing listings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If none is both quiet and near transit, the set helps identify the best compromise instead of matching each sales description alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93d88b0ec85364b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-69f2be7b04684526">Why can&#x27;t LLM relative reranking replace vector retrieval, or vice versa?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval cheaply builds a pool from a large catalog but can miss complex needs. LLM reranking compares a small pool in detail but cannot choose absent items. Set conditioning adds cost; local movies lack real dialogue and housing constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the best school-and-commute match misses the top 100, reranking explanations cannot restore it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69f2be7b04684526">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd070477da15b501">Why recompute Agg(X) whenever a real-estate candidate set changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It summarizes the current pool. Adding or removing listings changes relative budget and feasible options. Align structured fields and descriptions by identity and never choose candidates by real transaction labels. A local pointwise scorer is not full conversational reranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An initially cheap listing may cease to look cheap after adding lower-priced homes. The old mean misrepresents context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd070477da15b501">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:safro" data-paper-title="SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-926f0f190e18ffa3">Does each SAFRO rollout have one reward or several task rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>rᵢ,ₜ indexes candidate and task separately. A candidate can score differently on immediate interaction and long-term signals; preserve that matrix for comparisons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not treat two objectives on one item as two items on one objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:safro" data-paper-title="SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-20b5c57f1b03818c">Why normalize advantages within groups and across tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within-group ranking identifies better candidates for one objective; cross-task terms compare objectives for the same candidate. Relation gates organize search objectives, limiting domination by high-scale rewards without defining long-term value or guaranteeing joint gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalize dense clicks and sparse retention separately before balancing them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19585">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.19585-safro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20b5c57f1b03818c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:safro" data-paper-title="SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-467e8fa083cd8a30">Does standardization determine the relative importance of engagement and retention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It aligns scales, not business values. Relation gating combines goals without turning proxies into causal value. Specify reward definitions, axes, and fusion separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Standardizing two exams does not determine their graduation weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:safro" data-paper-title="SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-bfe6bd5eec699a5c">Does local SAFRO on MovieLens reproduce short-video retention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public full-catalog ranking tests proxy calculations, not private search, retention, or live buckets. Preserve negative results and do not call same-seed gaps online uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Offline movie hits are not next-day visits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-0ae30452731af4a0">Does ordered regression predict item IDs or cumulative behavior thresholds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It predicts whether a prefix reaches each click/payment count. Threshold and prefix-length axes are distinct; score the full prefix after adding a candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For three items, outputs can mean at least one or two clicks, not item identities.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef21fc2427c55791">Why estimate prefix value with ordered regression instead of summing item CTRs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item scores miss list interactions. Predict cumulative behavior thresholds after adding a candidate. Target queues narrow search, batched masks evaluate, and MMR participates during selection. Proxy labels and search bounds do not establish global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third similar phone may add less engagement than headphones despite higher standalone CTR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef21fc2427c55791">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choosing with marginal utility and similarity changes later prefixes. Removing duplicates only from the final list can leave holes or miss another generation trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting an early duplicate afterward does not recreate the alternative selection path.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-5765da49c1050335">Why model interference between ad positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two nearby large ads can compete for attention, so values are not independent.</p>

<h2 id="qa-62aed40bc12e6f28">Why check conflicts against the entire original sample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rounding probabilities derive from independent sampling under geometric and group constraints. Greedy acceptance changes conditional distributions. Local tests verify actual LP/rounding, not advertising uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accepting A first would change B&#x27;s decision; the paper instead evaluates both against one fixed sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85443f4bcd96a86e">How does LP with two-stage rounding differ from greedily placing ads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Solve the fractional program, test conflicts on the entire first-stage sample, then thin again. Greedy tests only already-kept items and changes probabilities and guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled item discarded later can still create a first-stage conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b1f33f48797fac">How handle disk boundaries and invalid probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cover only at strictly smaller distance than radius. Validate metric and thinning probabilities; fail rather than clip. Local HiGHS LP does not reproduce all auctions or the 2D PTAS.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Probability above one cannot be silently clipped without changing the distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-steps-e0be3966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc79db1d208005a2">Why decide both whether to push and when to wake again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed frequency ignores user state; polling wastes work. Planning, execution, and cheap filters jointly handle timing and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A no-send decision should still specify when to reevaluate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01949">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01949-steps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc79db1d208005a2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c92364d01f8e886f">Why use separate wake and send agents plus a filter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinal planning decides when to observe, trajectory reward drives sending, and a light filter rejects low-value or abnormal plans. This combines observation cadence and actions, without equating waiting value to message value or local ranking with retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Delay after an ignored notification, then still decline sending; filter one-second wake loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01949">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01949-steps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c92364d01f8e886f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c53833bd32479dc4">Are planning, execution, and filtering one threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Planning predicts wake interval, execution decides send, and filtering controls cost and anomalous plans. Combining them into one probability removes scheduling and guardrails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing tomorrow morning differs from choosing to send now.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01949">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01949-steps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c53833bd32479dc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-af395a3461d3e92d">Does local STEPS have real permissions and wall-clock wakeups?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens verifies decision decomposition, not push permissions, reach cost, clocks, or delivery. Actual service needs contracts and real rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating a simulated timestamp does not notify a phone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-swag-bid-1ae52cbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8e31735a2ad749a">Are SWAG-Bid episode boundaries and seven-day windows the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Episodes bound local interactions; the sliding window carries longer goals/state across episodes, not seven fixed actions. Do not reset all long-term context at every boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new bidding day does not restart a seven-day objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8e31735a2ad749a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d8d241ec0fb2ef2">Why use a seven-day plan across episodes and inject it through per-step gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local rewards can miss multi-day budgets. Sliding plans carry long goals; gates let immediate markets override guidance when appropriate. Masked future supervision is training-only, and a small zero-change result does not validate bidding gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Save budget during a crowded day but act on a valuable current opportunity using only available information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d8d241ec0fb2ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f09b12303391e18">How does masked future planning in training differ from deployment future access?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can construct masked plan signals under protocol. Serving sees only then-available state and estimates, not realized later GMV or spend.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tomorrow&#x27;s spend can supervise offline training but cannot be an input to today&#x27;s bid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f09b12303391e18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-73cfdb7c6e857295">Does local SWAG use real bids, budgets, and GMV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It ablates structure, not a production Decision Transformer. Maintain causal masks and timestamps, without filling from future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie action score is not an auction price.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
