<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-taiji-2fa562ab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f928cae1c771b93">Why use both semantic and collaborative-ID rewards in TAIJI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantics explains content, while IDs reflect platform interactions. They can conflict. Activate recommendation reasoning and balance goals dynamically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar descriptions need not imply co-preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f928cae1c771b93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-681897908cf2d793">Why dynamically balance semantic and collaborative rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different examples need different content/behavior trade-offs. Fixed directions can miss useful nonconvex solutions. Reverse preference reasoning and rejection sampling precede multiobjective alignment, without guaranteeing true preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cold item may rely on semantics while a popular one has rich interaction evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-681897908cf2d793">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3adb493a4a9fad7">How do dynamic Pareto weights differ from fixed linear weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed mixture covers one trade-off and can miss nonconvex frontiers. Dynamic weights adapt, but without comparisons they do not establish global Pareto optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user may value semantic novelty, another stable behavioral evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3adb493a4a9fad7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-45ec1fbe6228d174">How isolate rejection sampling and weight fitting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use permitted training preferences and validation; never use test feedback to choose reasoning or weights. Local MovieLens does not reproduce the real LLM, private codes, or serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting reasoning after reading a test click leaks the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45ec1fbe6228d174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uame-b8cd46d0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cbd00bc0c8913daa">Why predict a mean and variance in UAME?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple proxy scores can conflict. A Gaussian pair probability uses uncertainty during training, while serving reads only the mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High clicks and low watch can make relative preference less certain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cbd00bc0c8913daa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3dcc33d2640a4034">Why learn mean and variance, emphasize conflict in training, and serve only means?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gaussian score comparisons express proxy disagreement. Train using analytic wins, weight uncertain pairs, and regularize variance. Mean-only serving keeps cost low. Modeled uncertainty is not measured satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A click-friendly and a long-watch video create an uncertain pair; train on it but serve one mean score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3dcc33d2640a4034">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8588c89858fb0a5d">How does uncertainty weighting differ from averaging pxtr scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It emphasizes conflicting pairs and models comparison probability, unlike a fixed average. Variance is not observed satisfaction, and larger weights do not solve every conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two candidates strong on different metrics should not be collapsed without showing uncertainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8588c89858fb0a5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-d7048180b0074ee9">Does UAME sample Gaussian noise online, and how interpret local negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Serving uses mean only. Proxy losses do not reproduce author gains or refute private tests. Handle variance and zero-range weighting explicitly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal uncertainties give a zero min–max denominator; do not produce NaNs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-youtube-freshness-c4f4face" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d94c36948fa946f">Why separate training debiasing from serving exploration for freshness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Historical exposure favors old items. IPS/bias towers change learning signals, while uncertainty exploration changes actual exposures. Age features alone do not fix feedback loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old songs have more data because they were shown; new songs need actual opportunities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d94c36948fa946f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c80a24846ebefdf">Why separate debiasing and exploration instead of relying on freshness features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content age does not fix logged exposure selection. IPS and removable bias towers adjust training; SNGP uncertainty gives unknown items exposure online. Both depend on assumptions, and less head concentration does not prove satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new video may lack clicks because it has never been shown; explore and collect feedback rather than boosting all new videos blindly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c80a24846ebefdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-746a342e1a577d0e">How does a removable bias tower differ from retaining recency in serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A tower can absorb training exposure bias then be removed. Recency remains a serving signal. Do not keep adding learned exposure bias as quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning old items&#x27; logging advantage need not reward them again in deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-746a342e1a577d0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-1479c82e1a934ed5">Do local SNGP proxies or negative results explain YouTube&#x27;s live study?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. There is no full SNGP or continual training. Report interventions, logging propensities, and budgets separately. Popularity is not a measured IPS propensity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low popularity does not establish a low historical impression probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-8ddb1b3f7dfbb49a">Does RLBP use a neural network to bid in every auction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-rlbp">Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It chooses daily PID multipliers and writes a fixed daily lookup table; the original PID controls high-frequency feedback. Production varies P and I over three factors each with D=1, giving nine actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Set P to 1.2 times its default in the morning. Individual bids still respond to PID errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-c8f9a2fdc179857a">Why subtract the CPC head if CPC improvement is negative lift?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-rlbp">Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lower CPC is better and below-baseline change remains negative. In Qbu−beta×Qcpc, subtracting negative CPC raises the score. A multi-step CPC backup also uses min rather than max.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For equal budget score 0, CPC heads −0.1 and 0.2 with beta=1 give fused scores 0.1 and −0.2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33248v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33248-pinterest-rlbp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8f9a2fdc179857a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-fb6155c43c5dc6d6">Why can deployed RLBP behave like a contextual bandit despite the DQN name?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-rlbp">Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deployed gamma=0 regresses same-day outcomes with no future Q bootstrap. The proposed multi-step extension independently maxes/mins heads before fusion and need not equal optimal Q of the combined reward. It is not the deployed long-run optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reward 1, future Q 100: gamma 0 yields 1, whereas gamma 0.9 changes the objective to 91.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33248v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33248-pinterest-rlbp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb6155c43c5dc6d6">Question link</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-3a2389c12678fcb4">Does implementing top-K softmax reproduce production action probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-rlbp">Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Pinterest Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Production also needs trained Q, beta scale and post-fusion preprocessing. The component externalizes beta and preprocessing; identity is just a reference. Small tensor tests cannot supply logged propensities or actual outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Doubling scores often preserves top-K but sharpens softmax, changing IPS propensities despite the same argmax.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Why is sorting items by individual score not necessarily a good slate?

## Takeaway

Slate value depends on neighbors, position, and selected prefix. Redundancy-aware methods estimate marginal contribution. SORT-Gen uses prefix-conditioned multi-objective slate value. Policy methods trade off exploration, ad load, revenue, and long-term feedback. Titles, creatives, and layout affect exposure and belong in the evaluation. RLBP instead chooses bounded daily PID multipliers; two Q heads learn BU and CPC, then lifecycle weighting combines them. Similar objective weights do not imply identical states, actions, or rewards.

## Example

If three identical ski clips score 0.90, 0.89, and 0.88 and a camping clip scores 0.85, pointwise ranking chooses the first three. A slate model may choose the camping clip once duplicates have low marginal value. Whether this trade-off is worthwhile depends on objectives and constraints.

## Common pitfall

Weighted objectives do not guarantee hard ad-load or coverage constraints. Diversity does not guarantee satisfaction. MovieLens clicks, payments, or GMV proxies are mechanism evidence, not revenue. Long-term value needs a corresponding observation horizon.

## Reading order

Read CDM for relevance and redundancy, SORT-Gen for prefix-dependent value, and PRL-PUTS for prediction versus multi-objective policy. Check gaps between local proxies and production goals.

1. [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09021)
2. [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07197)
3. [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344)

## Check your understanding

If item-level CTR predictions stay identical, can reordering still change page clicks?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Yes. Position exposure, duplicate neighbors, and prefix effects can change slate outcomes despite unchanged pointwise scores.

</details>
